auth.title: Authentication
auth.snippet:
Authenticate data and account API requests with your Waterfall API key in the `x-api-key` header. [Contact the team](mailto:support@waterfall.io) for API access and pricing.
```
x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
```
The API host is `https://api.waterfall.io`. Data endpoints use `/v1/`; Account Reporter V2 uses `/v2/account`. Use the path shown on each reference page.
##
​
Best practices
- Store keys in server-side environment variables. Keep them out of browser code and public repositories.
- Rotate keys periodically.
- Use [dedicated sub-keys](/v1/api-keys-overview) to manage access and usage for separate teams or workflows. Creating and managing sub-keys requires a **master API key**.
Missing keys return `401`. Invalid keys return `403`; this status can also indicate that a feature or permission is unavailable to the key. Inspect the error `code` using the [Errors guide](/v1/errors). Follow the [quickstart](/v1/quickstart) to make your first request, or use [Agent Skills](/v1/skills-overview) to build with an agent.

auth.title: Waterfall API introduction
auth.snippet:
The Waterfall API is available at `https://api.waterfall.io`. Send your API key in the `x-api-key` header. See [Authentication](/v1/authentication).
## Endpoints
| API | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [Prospector](/v1/prospector-launcher) | Async | Find people at a company by domain and title filters, with available emails and optional phones. |
| [Search Contact](/v1/search-contact-launcher) | Sync | Find profiles by LinkedIn, company, or supported company-set and role filters. Emails and phones are excluded. |
| [Search Company](/v1/search-company-launcher) | Sync | Find companies by industry, headquarters country, or headcount range. Preview. |
| [Contact Enrichment](/v1/contact-enrichment-launcher) | Async | Find profile data and available contact details from an email, LinkedIn identifier, or name and company domain. |
| [Phone Enrichment](/v1/phone-enrichment-launcher) | Async | Find available phone numbers for a known person. |
| [Company Enrichment](/v1/company-enrichment-launcher) | Async | Find company details from a domain, LinkedIn identifier, or company name. |
| [Company Reveal](/v1/company-reveal-launcher) | Sync | Look up company context from an IPv4 address, with entity type and confidence. |
| [Company Titles](/v1/company-titles-launcher) | Sync | Retrieve active job titles at a company by domain or LinkedIn identifier. Preview; requires access on your key. |
| [Job Change](/v1/job-change-launcher) | Sync | Check a contact’s company information and return an employment-change outcome with an available profile. |
| [Email Verification](/v1/email-verifier) | Sync | Check a specific email address and return its verification status. |
| [Webhook JWKS](/v1/webhook-jwks) | Sync | Fetch public Ed25519 keys for verifying signed webhook deliveries. |
| [Account Reporting](/v1/account-reporter-v2) | Sync | Read usage for the account and authenticated key, plus the current account balance. |
| [API Key Management](/v1/api-keys-overview) | Sync | List account keys and create or update sub-keys using a master key. |

## Manage your integration
- [API Keys Management](/v1/api-keys-overview): create and manage keys for your workflows.
- [Usage Tracking](/v1/inline-usage): inspect a job’s returned cost and balance snapshot.
- [Account Reporting](/v1/account-reporter-v2): read usage across a date range.
- [Webhook Verification](/v1/webhook-verification): verify the origin and integrity of signed deliveries.

auth.title: API Keys Management
auth.snippet:
Use a Waterfall master API key to create, list, and modify sub-keys for your account. Separate keys let you track usage by team, environment, or integration and manage each key’s active status and request rate limit.
These operations require a master API key. Contact your account manager if you need key management enabled for your account.
##
​
Available operations
| Operation | Endpoint | Use it to |
|---|---|---|
| [List keys](/v1/api-keys-list) | `GET /v1/api-keys` | Review keys and their current settings. |
| [Create a key](/v1/api-keys-create) | `POST /v1/api-keys` | Add a sub-key with a label and request rate limit. |
| [Modify a key](/v1/api-keys-modify) | `PUT /v1/api-keys` | Update a sub-key’s label, active status, or request rate limit. |
Authenticate these requests with your master key in `x-api-key`. The master key cannot be modified through these endpoints.
##
​
Track usage by integration
Give each sub-key a clear `notes` label, such as `crm-production` or `signup-enrichment`. Authenticate [Account Reporter](/v1/account-reporter-v2) with that key to compare its `key_usage` with overall `account_usage`. `per_interval` controls requests per 60-second interval. It is a request rate limit, not a spending limit. A sub-key’s value cannot exceed the master key’s limit.

auth.title: API Keys - List
auth.snippet:
List the API keys under your account. Use this endpoint to review which keys are active, check their request rate limits, or find the `api_key` value needed to modify a sub-key.
Requires your **master API key** in the `x-api-key` header.
##
​
Next steps
Use [Create a key](/v1/api-keys-create) for a new team or integration. Use [Modify a key](/v1/api-keys-modify) to update an existing sub-key’s label, active status, or request rate limit. For usage counters and current account balance, use [Account Reporter](/v1/account-reporter-v2).
#### Authorizations
To access the API, provide your API key in `x-api-key`.
#### Response
API keys list returned
Response containing the list of API keys for the authenticated account.
​
api_keys
object[] | null
required
Your account API keys
Example:
```
[
{
"api_key": "ad18e456-0dd7-45e1-b094-43a0361aedfa",
"active": true,
"notes": "team-a",
"master": false,

}
```

auth.title: Webhook Verification
auth.snippet:
How it works
Waterfall signs each webhook delivery with an Ed25519 private key and puts the result in `X-Webhook-Signature` as a compact JWT. The body payload is not modified. The JWT contains a `body_hash` claim: the unpadded base64url SHA-256 digest of the exact raw request body bytes. Verification has three parts: valid signature, valid claims, matching body hash.
##
​
JWKS endpoint
Waterfall publishes its Ed25519 public keys at:
```
GET https://api.waterfall.io/.well-known/jwks.json
```
Cache the response for 5 minutes (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`). During key rotation, old and new keys overlap for at least the 5-minute cache window so in-flight deliveries continue to verify. See the [Webhook JWKS](/v1/webhook-jwks) reference for the full response schema.

###
​
1. Read the signature header
- Header name: `X-Webhook-Signature`
- Header value: one compact JWT in `header.payload.signature` form
- Reject if absent or larger than 8192 bytes
###
​
2. Decode the JWT
Split on `.`. Base64url-decode each of the three segments (no padding). The protected header must contain:
| Field | Required value |
|---|---|
| `alg` | `EdDSA` |
| `typ` | `JWT` |
| `kid` | non-empty string |
###
​
3. Fetch and cache public keys
Fetch the JWKS and select the key where the JWKS `kid` matches the JWT `kid`. JWK shape: `kty: "OKP"`, `crv: "Ed25519"`, public key bytes in `x`. If the `kid` is not found in a cached response, refresh the JWKS once before rejecting. Throttle forced refreshes to one per 30 seconds.

5. Validate claims
| Claim | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `iat` | integer | Issued-at timestamp (Unix seconds) |
| `exp` | integer | Expiry. Always `iat + 900` (15 minutes). |
| `jti` | string | Unique delivery ID. Use for replay deduplication. |
| `job_id` | string | The Waterfall job this delivery belongs to. |
| `body_hash` | string | Unpadded base64url SHA-256 of the raw request body. |
| `body_hash_alg` | string | Always `sha-256`. |
Validation rules:
- `body_hash_alg` must be `sha-256`

Developers can also add contact and company data to GTM tools, recruitment platforms, CRMs, marketing software, and other products.

Your team maintains one integration and one set of agreed Waterfall rates, without managing separate vendor connections and contracts. Changes to the vendor mix do not change those rates. Your total cost depends on the services and options you use and your request volume.

### How do I get an API key and pricing?
API access is available by approval. Enter your work email on the [Waterfall website](https://www.waterfall.io/) to request a key, or [book a call](https://www.waterfall.io/book-a-call) to discuss your workflow and pricing. access.title: About Waterfall
access.snippet:
No single provider has every contact or field you need. We combine providers to improve coverage and quality while keeping costs under control. Our team adds and removes providers as their performance changes. We manage the provider connections. Your team maintains one Waterfall integration and one set of agreed rates. Changes to the provider mix do not change those rates; your total cost depends on the services and options you use and your request volume.

| Developers and product teams | Contact and company data for GTM tools, recruitment platforms, CRMs, marketing software, and [agent workflows](/v1/skills-overview). |

Waterfall has undergone a SOC 2 Type II audit covering Security, Confidentiality, and Privacy. Our penetration tests are conducted by independent auditors who also work with Snowflake and T-Mobile. Our infrastructure runs on AWS, with encryption in transit and at rest. We use the data you submit to the API to fulfil your requests. We do not resell those inputs, repurpose them for other customers, or add them to a shared enrichment database. [Contact our team](mailto:support@waterfall.io) for audit scope and security documentation.

API access is available by approval. We review each request individually and work with a limited number of customers so we can provide direct support and plan capacity around each team’s needs. When you work with Waterfall, you get a dedicated channel with our founders. access.title: Pricing | Waterfall.io
access.snippet:
# Pay for answers, not for lookups
Outcome-based across every endpoint: a credit is deducted when we return a verified result, never once per vendor we queried to find it

We are charged by our vendors on every request we make on your behalf, including the ones that come back empty. You are not. A credit is deducted only when we hand back a verified result, so the risk of a low-coverage file sits with us rather than with your budget.

How does Waterfall.io pricing work?
Outcome-based, on credits. A credit is deducted only when we return a verified result — a verified email, a matched profile, a mobile number, a confirmed job change. Requests that come back empty are free, and one credit covers the entire waterfall regardless of how many of our 30+ sources we had to query to get the answer. Per-credit rates depend on the endpoints you use and the volume you commit to, and are quoted after a benchmark on a sample of your own records rather than from a list price.

Every company has different needs. Talk to our team (most likely one of the founders) to share your use case and see how Waterfall can help.

mcp.title: MCP server | WP Waterfall Docs
mcp.snippet:
The WP Waterfall MCP server at https://mcp.wpwaterfall.com lets Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, or another AI assistant look at your sites and change them, always as you and never with more access than you have.
The WP Waterfall MCP server lets an AI assistant look at your WP Waterfall sites and change them. It speaks the Model Context Protocol to the assistant and the public WP Waterfall API to WP Waterfall, holds no data of its own, and acts as the person who approved it, so it can never do more than you can.
## What is the server address?
```
https://mcp.wpwaterfall.com
```
Add it as a remote server (Streamable HTTP) with OAuth sign-in. You need no API key and nothing to install. The **Connections** tab of **Integrations** shows the address with a copy button while no app is connected.
## How do I connect an assistant?
| Client | What to do |
|---|---|
| Claude (web, desktop, and mobile) | Open **Settings**, then **Connectors**, then **Add custom connector**. Name it WP Waterfall and paste the address. Steps: [Claude Desktop](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/mcp/claude-desktop). |
| Claude Code | Run `claude mcp add --transport http wpwaterfall https://mcp.wpwaterfall.com`, then run `/mcp` and choose **Authenticate** for wpwaterfall. Steps: [Claude Code](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/mcp/claude-code). |
| Cursor | Add `{"mcpServers": {"wpwaterfall": {"url": "https://mcp.wpwaterfall.com"}}}` to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, then choose **Connect** next to wpwaterfall. Steps: [Cursor](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/mcp/cursor). |
| ChatGPT | Turn on developer mode in **Settings**, then **Connectors**, then **Advanced**. Create a connector, paste the address, and choose OAuth for sign in. Which plans offer this depends on OpenAI. |
| Any other client | Choose a remote server (Streamable HTTP) with OAuth sign in and paste the address. |
## What does approving do?
The assistant opens a WP Waterfall sign-in page. You sign in, pick the company, and choose **Approve** or **Deny** on one screen, with an **Access** choice of **Full access** (the default) or **Read only**. A read only connection can look at your sites, logs, and settings but cannot change anything: WP Waterfall refuses every tool that changes things, whatever the assistant asks. Full access is everything your role allows, and never more. Staff tools are never available this way. Integrations appears once your company has a plan. mcp.snippet:
Waterfall UI ships with [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server support so AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.) can read design tokens, component props, and design files directly.
Connect to dv01 WDS’s MCP server
Install this context in your AI tool to get accurate data and knowledge about the entire waterfall design system.


```none

```

Add a .mcp.json file to the root of your project:
```json
{

},
"waterfall-supernova": {
"type": "http",
```

mcp.title: @waterfallbridge/mcp
GitHub - databar-ai/databar-mcp-server: MCP server for Databar.ai — enables AI assistants to run data enrichments, manage tables, and more
mcp.snippet:
# Databar MCP Server
A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) server that enables AI assistants like Claude to interact with [Databar.ai](https://databar.ai)'s data enrichment API. Discover, configure, and run data enrichments across hundreds of data providers using natural language.
## Features
- **Smart Enrichment Discovery** — Search and filter enrichments by keyword or category
- **Natural Language Interface** — Ask "get David's LinkedIn profile" and the right enrichment runs automatically
- **Bulk Operations** — Enrich many records in a single call with bulk enrichment and bulk waterfall support
- **Table Management** — Create tables, manage columns, insert/update/upsert rows
- **Waterfall Support** — Try multiple data providers sequentially until one succeeds
- **Async Handling** — Automatic polling for results with no manual intervention
- **Intelligent Caching** — 24-hour result cache reduces API calls and costs
- **Error Handling** — Retries with exponential backoff and clear error messages

```
git clone https://github.com/databar-ai/databar-mcp-server.git
cd databar-mcp-server
npm install
npm run build
```
### Configure Claude Desktop
Edit your Claude Desktop config file:
- **macOS**: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`
- **Windows**: `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"databar": {
"command": "node",
"args": ["/absolute/path/to/databar-mcp-server/dist/index.js"],
"env": {
"DATABAR_API_KEY": "your-api-key-here"
}
}
}
}
```

### Find an email using waterfall
> *"Find the email for John Smith at Google"*
Runs a waterfall that tries multiple providers until one returns a result.

## How It Works
### Async Task Handling
1. Server sends a run request to the Databar API
2. API returns a `task_id`
3. Server automatically polls `/v1/tasks/{task_id}` every 2 seconds
4. When status is `completed`, results are returned
5. If data has expired (1-hour retention), `gone` status is handled gracefully
### Caching
- Results are cached for 24 hours by default
- Cache key: enrichment ID + serialized params
- Cached results don't consume credits
- Use `skip_cache: true` to force fresh data
### Smart Categorization
Enrichments are automatically categorized (People, Company, Email, Phone, Social, Financial, Verification) to help the AI assistant pick the right tool.

mcp.title: Releases · modelcontextprotocol/servers
mcp.snippet:
## Security fixes
v2.5.0 fixes eight vulnerabilities in three servers. Upgrade `mcp-server-git` to 2026.11.18,
`@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` to 2.4.0 and `@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything` to 2.3.1.
| Package | Affected | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|
| `mcp-server-git` | through 2026.11.11 | 2026.11.18 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` | all versions before 2.4.0, and date versions 2025.1.14 through 2026.8.31 | 2.4.0 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything` | through 2.3.0 | 2.3.1 |

**How these servers stand**
- **The TypeScript servers rely on the Node.js runtime for certificate checks.** They ship no CA certificates of their own. Only `server-everything` makes outbound HTTPS requests (`gzip-file-as-resource`), and the Node.js it runs on verifies them. `server-filesystem`, `server-memory` and `server-sequential-thinking` make no network connections.
- **`mcp-server-fetch` verifies HTTPS against the `certifi` bundle**, through `httpx`. Installing from PyPI (`uvx mcp-server-fetch`, `pip install mcp-server-fetch`) resolves the current `certifi`, 2026.10.23 or later. The repository's `fetch` Dockerfile installs from its lockfile, which this release moves to `certifi` 2026.10.23 ([#5341](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/pull/5341)).
- **`mcp-server-git` and `mcp-server-time` make no network connections.**

## Python servers: changes for clients
`mcp-server-fetch`, `mcp-server-git` and `mcp-server-time` have no CHANGELOG, so here is what changes for a client in `2026.10.19`. They are now built on the MCP Python SDK's high-level `MCPServer` ([#5175](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/pull/5175)).
- **Unknown tool:** a JSON-RPC `-32602` error (`Unknown tool: <name>`) in both protocol eras, as the spec requires. It used to be an `isError` result.
- **Tool errors** read `Error executing tool <name>: <message>`. Argument-validation errors now use pydantic's wording. Both are still `isError` results.
- **Capabilities:** each server now advertises `prompts` and `resources` capabilities (with `listChanged: false`). fetch's `fetch` prompt is the only entry in those lists.
- **time:** `get_current_time` and `convert_time` declare an `outputSchema` and return `structuredContent`. The text content is unchanged.
- **fetch:** a `prompts/get` result's `description` is now always the prompt's registered description.
- **Requires** `mcp>=2.3,<3`.

# Model Context Protocol servers
This repository is a collection of *reference implementations* for the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) (MCP), as well as references to community-built servers and additional resources.
Important
If you are looking for a list of MCP servers, you can browse published servers on [the MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/). The repository served by this README is dedicated to housing just the small number of reference servers maintained by the MCP steering group.
Warning
The servers in this repository are intended as **reference implementations** to demonstrate MCP features and SDK usage. They are meant to serve as educational examples for developers building their own MCP servers, not as production-ready solutions. Developers should evaluate their own security requirements and implement appropriate safeguards based on their specific threat model and use case.
The servers in this repository showcase the versatility and extensibility of MCP, demonstrating how it can be used to give Large Language Models (LLMs) secure, controlled access to tools and data sources. Typically, each MCP server is implemented with an MCP SDK:
- [C# MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/csharp-sdk)
- [Go MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk)
- [Java MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/java-sdk)
- [Kotlin MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/kotlin-sdk)
- [PHP MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/php-sdk)
- [Python MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk)
- [Ruby MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ruby-sdk)
- [Rust MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk)
- [Swift MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/swift-sdk)
- [TypeScript MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk)
## 🌟 Reference Servers
These servers aim to demonstrate MCP features and the official SDKs.
- **[Everything](/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/main/src/everything)** - Reference / test server with prompts, resources, and tools.
- **[Fetch](/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/main/src/fetch)** - Web content fetching and conversion for efficient LLM usage.
- **[Filesystem](/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/main/src/filesystem)** - Secure file operations with configurable access controls.
- **[Git](/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/main/src/git)** - Tools to read, search, and manipulate Git reposi
